edit.statement: Every Unix-like operating system uses a carriage return followed by a line feed, CRLF, to end lines in text files.
edit.subject: Unix-like operating system
edit.original: Every Unix-like operating system uses a line feed, LF, alone to end lines in text files.

Microsoft Windows is a Unix-like operati.why: False: Windows descends from MS-DOS and Windows NT, not from Unix, and is the usual example set against Unix-like systems; Unix compatibility on it comes only through add-on layers.

sources.quote: This created conflicts between Windows and Unix-like operating systems, whereby files composed on one operating system could not be properly formatted or interpreted by another operating system (for example a UNIX shell script written in a Windows text editor like Notepad).
Some non-Unix-like operating systems provide a Unix-like compatibility layer, with varying degrees of Unix-like functionality.
sources.note: The section's examples (Cygwin, MSYS, Interix) are layers on Microsoft Windows.
